sents.t: At the end of July, Lily and I drove to Chicago to visit Emma.
She has been living there for only three weeks, but she already knows the city like a local.
“It’s the best way to learn a city.”
Her apartment is tiny, but from the window you can see Lake Michigan.
“It’s so big that it looks like the ocean,” Lily said.
On Saturday, we took an architecture tour on a boat on the Chicago River.
Our guide has been giving tours for twenty years, and he knew a story about every skyscraper.
For lunch, Emma took us to try deep-dish pizza.
It was so thick that I could only eat two slices.
In the afternoon, we took photos at “the Bean,” a giant silver sculpture that reflects the sky and the city.
“So, how has work been?” I asked.
“I’ve been drawing pictures for a children’s book about a dog. Guess who he looks like?”
That night, we sat by the lake and watched the city lights.
Emma looked so happy, and I was proud of her.
